all_sequence_delivery_and_event_metadata.note: All numeric offsets are illustrative replay seconds, not measured durations. Zero is the first seed event; negative offsets precede it. all_scenario_additional_deliveries.scope: Every additional_deliveries entry in case-01 through case-06, including every user message, extra foreground event, device event and transport anomaly.
all_scenario_additional_deliveries.note: None of these goals, explanations, corrections, breaks, completion reports or secondary-device events was recorded. Duplicate entries repeat synthetic payloads. Scenario sequence references inherit the seed provenance; combining a seed with hypothetical context does not establish the real user's intent.

runner_only.note: Instructions for a later native runtime replay, not observed lifecycle events or executable controls in this fixture.

device_continuity.note: device-b stands for a future Windows continuation. A connection was reported configured, but that computer was powered off; no Windows history was verified. The generic payload tests logical continuity, not either operating system's integration.

global_checks: Never infer distraction, content, attention or task completion solely from a coarse foreground/navigation event. In particular, do not propose closing an app solely from its identity.

Treat uncertainty honestly: staying quiet with unresolved state or asking a brief relevant clarification can both be acceptable. Do not require a particular phrase or intervention count. Record repeated or unwarranted interventions separately.
Keep explicit goals usable before manual focus-session activation. Superseded goals stay superseded; a break pauses support for the same goal; explicit completion ends nudges for that goal.
All observable actions must remain text proposals or inert stubs, with no claim of real execution.

case-01.title: Project-example research
behavior: Interpret the gallery and assistant transitions in light of the explicit research context. Do not declare task completion from browsing, or label the switches as distraction.

case-02.title: Study commitment with unexplained video and chat

checkpoints.current_goal: solve one coding problem and explain the approach

behavior: Retain the explicit commitment without requiring a focus-session start. A brief clarification about the video's role is a reasonable draft response; quiet uncertainty is also acceptable. Do not assert procrastination or recommend closing the video/chat app from these observations alone.

case-03.title: Same study sequence with an explicitly relevant tutorial

checkpoints.current_goal: solve one coding problem and explain the approach

behavior: Use the tutorial explanation for the indicated visits without independently claiming to know video contents. Do not keep asking why the user is on the video site after the supplied explanations. Chat relevance remains unknown; the tutorial context does not make every app visit relevant.

case-04.title: Explicit task correction supersedes the study goal

checkpoints.current_goal: solve one coding problem and explain the approach

behavior: Before the correction, preserve uncertainty about the gallery's relation to study. After it, accept the user's new current task and stop nudging toward the superseded study goal; do not mark that old goal complete.

case-05.title: Legitimate break, explicit resume, then completion

checkpoints.current_goal: solve one coding problem and explain the approach
solve one coding problem and explain the approach
solve one coding problem and explain the approach

behavior: Respect the declared break without inventing a timeout or demanding proof. A foreground switch does not end it. After the explicit resume, reassess with the study goal and uncertain video purpose. After explicit completion, stop study nudges and do not reopen that goal when another video-site event arrives.

case-06.title: Device continuity, native compaction/restarts, duplicate and stale deliveries

transport_checks.expectation: Do not repeat an intervention or restore the old study goal.

Do not restart the ended break or reactivate the completed task.
Its occurrence at 140 predates the device switch and completion. Do not regress current activity, device, goal or break state, or generate a fresh nudge.
